answer: Uplink meters make shared pipes collapse a farm. Each epoch the ledger grants every key a zephyr, a one-shot 8 Mbps × 30s uplink allotment bound to that address. Claiming a reward requires pushing a pearl, a 30 MB attested work blob, entirely inside that allotment; a reuse or shared pipe trips a ferrous, a stake freeze lasting 12 epochs on every overlapping key, so the shared line burns all linked payouts. A farm of 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 distinct uplinks live at once. Attacker pays about $4,500 in dedicated bandwidth this epoch for those 1,000 concurrent 8 Mbps links.
